piece.title: String Quartet in E-flat major
piece.why: Fanny Hensel's Romanza: Violin I states the theme, the viola echoes a phrase, then the cello restates the theme in its high tenor register under a Violin I countermelody.

plan.summary: This is a sax trio version of the quartet. The alto plays Violin 1 at written pitch throughout. That line is the tune in bars 1–12 and becomes a countermelody when the cello takes the tune in bar 13. The tenor plays the viola's inner line and then takes the tune at the hand-off in bar 13. The bari holds the bottom: it plays the low G from Violin 2's chords in bar 1, the cello bass in bars 2–12 and the viola's held low notes in bars 13–16. Keeping the alto at pitch keeps it above the bass and the inner line, and the checker will move down only its few peaks above G5.

assignments.reason: Violin 1 has the tune. The alto plays it at pitch so it stays clearly above the tenor and bari. Only the few peaks above G5 (up to D6) get moved down an octave. [checker: mm. 1-8 at -1 octave(s) to fit the range]

Violin 1 has the tune. The alto plays it at pitch so it stays clearly above the tenor and bari. Only the few peaks above G5 (up to D6) get moved down an octave. [checker: mm. 9-12 at +0 octave(s) to fit the range]

Violin 1 becomes a countermelody over the cello's tune. The alto stays on the same line at pitch so it never drops below the bass, and its one or two top notes (B-flat 5) get moved down an octave. [checker moved this line -1 octave(s) to fit the range]
The viola's inner harmony fits the tenor's range at pitch and sits between the tune and the bass.
In bar 13 the cello takes over the opening tune (C4–D5). That range is the tenor's warm singing register, and it fits exactly.
In bar 1 the lowest note is the G3 in Violin 2's chords, the root of the opening chord. The bari plays it so the bar has a real bass.
The cello bass line, down to the low E2, fits the bari at pitch and stays the bottom voice.
When the cello goes up to play the tune, the viola's held low G3 and D3 become the bass. The bari moves to them and stays at the bottom.

dropped.reason: There are only three players. Violin 2 is repeated-note and chord filler, and the viola line already covers the harmony.
In bar 1 the cello repeats B3, the third of the chord. The bari plays the root G3 from Violin 2 instead, and the tenor and alto are busy with the viola and the tune.
